topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and states what students should learn.

topics.label: Genetic origins and clonal evolution of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arise and enable susceptible cells to evolve into cancers within a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and the interpretation of causal evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence about environmental contributions to cancer should be interpreted rather than reduced to chance or genetic predisposition.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections contribute to carcinogenesis, with Burkitt lymphoma developing the general account into a detailed case study.

topics.label: Mechanisms of DNA damage from environmental carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce potentially mutagenic DNA damage through processes that depend on their interaction with the body.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish acquiring initiating mutations from promoting the growth of mutated cells and explain why both processes matter for tumour development.

topics.label: Context-dependent susceptibility and recap of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: The discussion of susceptibility at particular developmental stages leads into a recap of how carcinogenic effects depend on the context of exposure.

topics.label: Evidence linking carcinogen exposure to human cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how evidence collected from human populations and their biological samples can link carcinogen exposure to cancer.

topics.label: Experimental carcinogenicity testing and its limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how experimental tests assess carcinogenic potential and why their results cannot fully reproduce cancer development in humans.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit perspective
topics.groupedBecause: This closing consolidates the lecture's main lessons into a final perspective on everyday risk–benefit decisions.
